overall_assessment: Iteration 1 established a foundation but has critical gaps. Only 1 of 4 data gathering methods is fully operational (DG-0001 web search). The Wikipedia and arXiv methods have API connectivity issues that must be resolved before the hybrid method can demonstrate its cross-referencing value. Code quality is decent across all methods (75-82/100) but robustness is the primary weakness (35-72/100). Team 1's research is high quality (A-) but needs to be more actionable — it describes what tools exist but not how to programmatically access them. The improvement loop architecture is sound; Team 3 needs to prioritize fixing existing methods over building new ones. Three new methods are recommended for iteration 2: Semantic Scholar, FRED, and GitHub search.
loop_health_justification: Yellow because: (1) 3 of 4 methods are broken/degraded, (2) the core value proposition of the hybrid method (cross-source corroboration) is untestable, (3) Team 1's research quality is strong but needs translation into actionable implementation specs. The loop architecture itself is healthy — all teams produced useful output and the feedback mechanisms are working. Upgrading to green requires: fixing DG-0002 and DG-0003, and having at least 3 methods return meaningful results.
